clue.text: Suffer acute embarrassment withholding right to primary education

indicators.note: the setter's word withholding splits into with plus holding, and holding says the word with keeps something inside it
primary means first, so only the opening letter of education is used

explanation.surface: Someone squirms with shame at being denied a child's basic schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withholding' must be split into WITH + 'holding': WITH holds R to give WRITH, then E, the first letter of education, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, as a person does when mortified.

clue.text: He brings back news concerning carrier

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a porter carries luggage

explanation.surface: A messenger returns with word about a postman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings back' is not a reversal; it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter gathers and relays news to a paper.

clue.text: The shape of a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Describing the outline of something in the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided figure and also a percussion instrument of bent steel.

clue.text: No. sixteen undergoing alterations -new rooms added

indicators.note: undergoing alterations says the letters are being changed round

parts.note: the full stop is ignored, leaving the letters NO

explanation.surface: Number 16 is being rebuilt and extended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undergoing alterations' is the anagram signal on NO SIXTEEN; 'alterations' also suits the building surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an addition built onto a house.

clue.text: Official language

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat's jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a high official of imperial China, and Mandarin is also the main spoken form of Chinese.

clue.text: Sadly interred Michael, the entertainer

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A performer named Michael has been buried, alas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like mourning but signals an anagram of INTERRED MICHAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-born film star and cabaret singer.

clue.text: Dr. Foster wasn't in the first rank of doctors, really — you should hear other doctors!

definitions.text: Dr. Foster wasn't in the first rank of doctors, really — you should hear other doctors!

parts.words: Dr. Foster wasn't in the first rank of doctors, really — you should hear other doctors!
parts.note: the nursery rhyme's Doctor Foster went to Gloucester and stepped in a puddle up to his middle, so his feet got soaked; the jokey rest pretends to judge his medical standing

explanation.surface: Colleagues sneer that Dr Foster was never a top physician.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Foster is from a British nursery rhyme: he went to Gloucester in a shower of rain and stepped in a puddle, so he was not dry-footed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry-shod means with dry feet, never wetting them.

clue.text: Favour displaying a lot of Yorkshire's emblems

indicators.note: displaying says the letters are on show in the words, and a lot of says not all of them are used

explanation.surface: A preference shows in the many symbols of a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' is used in the sense of looking like a parent: 'she favours her father'.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour a relative is to look like them, a dated or regional usage.

clue.text: Mine is among the votes against the candidates

indicators.note: is among puts one word inside another

parts.note: the noes are those voting against a motion

explanation.surface: My vote is one of those opposing the contenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' is taken as written and placed inside NOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominees are people put forward for a post or prize.

clue.text: Athlete coming second to pressman

parts.note: a pressman works a printing press, so is a printer

explanation.surface: A runner finishes runner-up behind a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressman' looks like a reporter, but here it is the man who runs the press; 'coming ... to' just puts S before PRINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is a track runner over short distances.

clue.text: Mineral responsible for pain, some say

indicators.note: some say signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'; taken as written before being spoken

explanation.surface: A rock is blamed for causing someone discomfort, so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: GYP is informal British for pain or trouble; 'gyp some' spoken aloud gives the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is a soft calcium sulphate rock used to make plaster.

clue.text: Guns-one is out of order

indicators.note: is out of says the letter for one leaves the word for order

parts.note: an ordinance is an official order or decree
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A weapon fails: one gun is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' reads as broken; in fact 'order' is ORDINANCE, and I (one) drops out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means artillery and military weapons collectively.

clue.text: Witch-doctor succeeded a fellow who was hanged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
Haman, in the Book of Esther, was hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai

explanation.surface: A tribal healer took over from a man who was executed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer believed to deal with spirits.

clue.text: Gnarled old tree I hung around

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker lingered by a twisted ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnarled' is the anagram signal on OLD TREE I.
explanation.definitionFit: Loitered means lingered idly, with no purpose.

clue.text: Forceful, upstanding citizen — for instance, Descartes

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue says the whole run is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: cit is a short form of citizen
e.g. abbreviates for example
René Descartes was the French philosopher

explanation.surface: A vigorous, honest man, such as a French thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' looks like a compliment but reverses CIT + EG + RENE, giving ENERGETIC read downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic means vigorous and forceful.

clue.text: Release without charge

explanation.surface: Letting someone go without a fee or prosecution.
explanation.definitionFit: To free is to release; free also means costing nothing.

clue.text: Conifers produce these

indicators.note: produce here hints that the letters of conifers are made into something new

explanation.surface: Evergreen trees bear their seed-cases.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: conifers do produce cones, and the anagram of CONIFERS gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fir cones are the woody seed-bearing structures of fir trees.

clue.text: Mountain ridge entraps detective climbing with others

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue says the letters are read upwards, so backwards
entraps says the ridge holds the detective inside it

parts.note: an arete is a sharp mountain ridge
tec is a short form of detective

explanation.surface: A ridge traps a detective who is scaling it alongside companions.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means read upwards; it turns the whole ridge-with-detective unit, giving ET CET ERA. 'Entraps' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera, Latin for 'and the rest', means and other things besides.

clue.text: Hardens heart of pernicious fly

indicators.note: heart of keeps only the middle, dropping the first and last letters of the insect named

parts.note: the tsetse is an African fly that spreads sleeping sickness

explanation.surface: Something toughens the core of a dangerous insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of pernicious' looks like the middle of that word; the heart is taken from TSETSE, the harmful fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets means becomes firm, as jelly or concrete does.

clue.text: Eating too much forcemeat

explanation.surface: Gorging on sausage meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffing oneself is overeating; stuffing is also the seasoned filling put inside a roast.

clue.text: Wealth accumulated when old city invested in timber

indicators.note: invested in says something is placed inside, with a financial flavour

parts.note: a tree is a source of timber
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Riches were built up when an ancient city put money into wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested in' reads as finance but is the container signal; UR is a favourite crossword old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a hoard of riches gathered over time.

clue.text: Poor soldier turned the wrong way, interrupting order

indicators.note: interrupting says one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: an indent is an official order for goods

indicators.note: turned the wrong way says the word for soldier is written backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A penniless soldier did an about-turn and disrupted the drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned the wrong way' reverses the soldier to IG; 'order' here is the commercial sense, an order for supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means destitute, lacking the necessities of life.

clue.text: Inspired one Edward to imprison Henry

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to imprison says one name is locked inside another

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edward
Hal is a pet form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: An Edward was moved to jail a Henry, as English kings did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' means breathed in, not motivated.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is, literally, to draw breath into the lungs.

clue.text: Small child in Indian nursery

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation within the tribe's name

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
small asks for the abbreviation CH for child

explanation.surface: A little one attends a nursery school in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' means a Native American people, the Cree, not India.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a day nursery for small children.

clue.text: Hard struggle for small naval vessel?

explanation.surface: A tough fight over a tiny warship.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase as a tug of a warship: a small boat belonging to the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug-of-war is a rope-pulling contest, hence any hard contest; a tug is a small boat, and a man-of-war a naval ship.

clue.text: Do the French have to nag?

parts.note: to need to is to have to
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Asks whether French people must pester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' just frames the question; NEED (have to) and LE (French 'the') make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or pester them persistently.

clue.text: Plotting ruin, I get frustrated

indicators.note: frustrated suggests plans thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schemer admits that being thwarted makes them angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frustrated' is the anagram signal on RUIN I GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrigue is secret scheming against someone.

clue.text: Careless hit-and-run

parts.note: a slap is a hit with the open hand
a dash is a short run

explanation.surface: A reckless driver strikes and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit-and-run' looks like a driving offence, but splits into hit and run.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash means hasty and careless.

clue.text: By the sound of it, ring a bird

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for ring is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a signet is a ring bearing a seal

explanation.surface: Ringing a bird, apparently, as an ornithologist tags it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring a bird' suggests tagging it; really SIGNET (ring) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan.
